summary:
An offline first sky and weather app for farmers.

StarCrop identifies constellations and stars, shows the upcoming weather, and turns both into practical farming guidance for when to plant, spray, or harvest. Everything works without internet. Only the weather download needs signal, and the last forecast is kept on the phone.
details:
StarCrop matches the current sky and the cached forecast to farming rules and shows guidance in a language farmers use. The sky view is calculated from the user's location and the time, not the camera, so it works in daylight, under cloud, and indoors. An AR overlay draws the constellations over the live camera view and moves them as the phone turns, so farmers can find them and learn their local names. Each rule shows its source (farmer, extension office, or publication) and a status of draft, reviewed, or confirmed. It complements DA (Department of Agriculture) and DOST (Department of Science and Technology) advisories by making such information usable offline, alongside local knowledge.

Status. The app is built and working: offline sky view with a live AR constellation overlay, cached forecast, and rule-based guidance for rice and coconut. What it lacks is data: verified farming rules and documented local names and terms, which require research.

Technology. Mobile software with an augmented reality (AR) constellation overlay and an offline rules engine, licensed to institutions.

Primary SDG: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger). Secondary: SDG 13 (Climate Action) and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure).

The Problem

Aklan farmers decide when to plant, spray, and harvest under heavy weather risk, with little reliable information and weak rural internet.

  • Information gap: about half of farmers and fisherfolk reported no source of farm information in 2019, and under 5% used the internet (DA baseline study, national).
  • Connectivity: 36.1% of rural households had used the internet in the previous three months, versus 57.3% of urban households (National ICT Household Survey, 2019).
  • Weather risk: Typhoon Ursula (2019) hit Aklan and Capiz, and Tropical Depression Agaton (2018) flooded six Aklan municipalities along the Aklan River.

Local sky knowledge, such as the Visayan use of the Pleiades to mark the seasonal calendar, is rarely documented or searchable.

Target Users


Primary users are smallholder rice, coconut, and vegetable farmers in Aklan, especially where signal or extension access is weak. Rice covers 42,218 hectares in Aklan and coconut 32,276 hectares. Nationally, about 68.5% of farmers cultivate two hectares or less and nearly three-fifths are aged 50 and above, so older farmers are often helped by younger household members. StarCrop is designed for the helper as well as the farmer.

Value Proposition

  • Works without a signal, in familiar language, with a source and verification status on every rule. This addresses the inconsistent government advice noted in the PIDS study.
  • Weather information is valued. Farmers in Dingle, Iloilo were willing to pay PHP 233.55 once for better local weather information (Lacson et al., 2020).
  • Local knowledge is preserved and made searchable alongside scientific forecasts.

Business Model

StarCrop stays free for farmers, which protects adoption and its trust system. Revenue comes from licensing and partnerships with institutions that deliver its offline content to farmers they already serve: provincial and municipal agriculture offices (app plus a regional rule pack), farmer cooperatives, telecom operators (bundled value-added content), and NGOs or development programmes (funded pilots). Named potential partners include the Office of the Provincial Agriculturist and Aklan State University. Licence pricing will be set after the pilot using partner feedback and usage data.

Market Analysis

About 6.05 million farmers and 0.9 million fisherfolk operate nationally (DA, 2021). The serviceable market in Aklan, farmers with smartphones in unreliable-signal areas who would use the app, has not yet been quantified, and the pilot will provide the first measured estimate. Existing tools cover parts of the problem: PhilRice's Rice Crop Manager (SMS in Filipino, the main widely adopted advisory), DA and DOST advisories, Stellarium Mobile (sky only), and Plantix and FarmSense (diagnosis and fertilizer). StarCrop's difference is the combination of offline sky, cached weather, and sourced local rules with visible verification.
